sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Kentucky, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Tuesday, October 20Passed

The last day to ask for a mail-in absentee ballot was Tuesday, October 20, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (the rule: your request must be received 14 days before the election). That deadline has passed. If you or your spouse has a medical emergency within 14 days of the election, the State Board's page describes a notarized application to the county clerk; ask your county clerk whether it can still help you. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your mail-in absentee ballot must be received by your county clerk by 6 p.m. local time on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A postmark is not enough. The state urges you not to wait until Election Day to hand it in. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Saturday, October 31, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Kentucky’s own site

At school away from home, in Kentucky or in another state? What Kentucky says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Yes, you need one of the reasons the law lists to get a ballot by mail. They include: you will be out of your county on Election Day and on every day of in-person absentee and early voting; you are a student living outside your home county; you live outside Kentucky for a while but can still vote here; you cannot get to the polls because of age, disability or illness; you are a military or overseas voter; you are in the state's address-protection program for crime victims; or you are in jail charged with a crime but not convicted. The State Board's page also describes a notarized application for a voter (or their spouse) who has a medical emergency within 14 days of the election; ask your county clerk about it. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Ask for a mail-in absentee ballot on the State Board of Elections' online portal. Open it (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it to your county clerk. It must arrive by 6 p.m. local time on Election Day. (official page)
  • Drop box. Every county has a drop box where you can hand deliver your ballot. The State Board of Elections' website shows where your county's drop box is. (official page)
  • In person. You (or a person the law allows) may hand it in at the county clerk's office in the county where you are registered, or at a secure drop-off box the clerk keeps. (the law)

What the envelope needs

No witness is described. You sign the envelope, and the county clerk compares your signature. If the signature does not match, the clerk mails you a form (SBE 77) so you can fix it, and your ballot is counted once the completed form comes back. (the law)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Kentucky’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Thursday, October 29, 2026 to Saturday, October 31, 2026.

Anyone can vote early in person, no reason needed, on Thursday, October 29, Friday, October 30 and Saturday, October 31, 2026. Before that, voters with one of the law's reasons (for example a student living outside their home county, a voter who is pregnant in the last trimester, a worker scheduled through all voting hours, or someone who cannot get to the polls because of age, disability or illness) can vote an excused in-person absentee ballot on October 21, 22, 23, 26, 27 and 28, 2026. The State Board's site lists your county's times and places. (official page)

Students

At school in Kentucky, away from home

A Kentucky student living on campus outside their home county may ask for an absentee ballot mailed to their on-campus address. Being a student who lives outside your home county for a while is one of the law's reasons for a mail-in ballot, and the ballot must be mailed to the address where you live for school (for November 3, 2026 the request deadline, October 20, has passed). Students away from their county can also vote in person on the excused absentee days if they will be gone on Election Day and the early-voting days. Kentucky law places your voting residence where your home is. (official page)

At school in another state, with Kentucky as home

A Kentucky resident going to school in another state or abroad who wants to vote in Kentucky can ask for an absentee ballot sent to their college address. You must ask again for every election you are away. Students from other states going to school in Kentucky can register in Kentucky, or contact their home state's election office to vote there. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military members and their families, and Kentucky citizens living outside the United States, register and ask for a ballot with the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA). Your county clerk must receive it no later than 7 days before the election: Tuesday, October 27, 2026. Your voted ballot must reach the county clerk by the close of polls on Election Day (6 p.m. local time, November 3, 2026). You can track your ballot in the Voter Information Center. The Federal Voting Assistance Program explains the federal process and forms. (official page)

Kentucky in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The deadline to ask for a mail-in ballot for November 3, 2026 passed on October 20. If you are not able to get one, Kentucky's excused in-person absentee days (October 21 to 28) and no-excuse early voting days (October 29 to 31) are still ahead.
  • The State Board's mail-in page links only the online portal for asking for a mail-in ballot; its Voters with Disabilities page also says to visit the portal or call your county clerk.
  • Voters with disabilities can ask their county clerk for a ballot through the state's Disability Absentee Portal: the ballot is marked online (mouse, keyboard or a compatible device) or printed, and must be printed and returned to the county clerk's office by 6 p.m. on Election Day (State Board of Elections, Voters with Disabilities page).

How this was checked

  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program page loads by script and could not be read; it is linked, not quoted.

Polls are open 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. local time. (source)

  • rest of the state: 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. EST
  • Western Kentucky: 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. CST

Anyone in line when the polls close may still vote.
